attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, introduced with 'I fully believe'.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the words. In context, the claim is that no collapse has yet acted as a 'wake-up call': it is about a missing trigger and implies a counterfactual.

contract.note: The contract treats 'only reason' as a claim that nothing else drives investment, so any stated driver contradicts it. The speaker says the boom continues because no collapse has stopped it, and that 'psychosis' drives it. That reading leaves room for firms to cite performance. The contract sets aside the counterfactual, which is the heart of the claim.

evidence.note: Alphabet's own account of why it invests. This is a company disclosure, not an independent finding. It does not show what investment would have been if OpenAI had collapsed, so it cannot settle the speaker's counterfactual claim.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm causal claim. On a fair reading it says the boom has lasted because no OpenAI collapse has ended it. The only evidence is Alphabet stating its own reasons for investing. That cannot establish or rule out the counterfactual, and the packet itself admits this gap. Treating a company's self-stated driver as a contradiction depends on the contract's exclusive-cause reading, which stretches the claim against the speaker.

attribution.note: Zitron's own firm statement in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'Will be a direct result' predicts a future collapse and names its causes. It should be filed as a forecast, not a backward-looking causal claim. No deadline is given; nearby text says 'can't say when'.

contract.note: The support and contradiction conditions both require a real collapse and then test whether the named causes produced it. That is fair. It is wrongly labelled retrospective and causal; it is really a prospective forecast.

evidence.note: Oracle's 27 Oct 2026 announcement shows OpenAI still working with partners. No collapse has happened, and a company announcement says nothing about future financial viability.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. OpenAI had not collapsed by the evaluation date, so the causes of a collapse cannot be judged. A forecast with no deadline does not fail just because the event has not yet happened.

attribution.note: Zitron's own unhedged statement in his newsletter.

semantics.note: A firm present-tense claim that LLMs bring no measurable ROI or productivity benefit, and do not do what their makers promised. 'In any way measurable' makes it categorical.

contract.note: Reading 'in any way measurable' as a flat denial is an ordinary reading. Taking April–June 2026 as the period is the evaluator's choice. The result depends on accepting pull requests per developer as a measure of productivity. The promises clause cannot be scored.

evidence.note: Preprint measuring April 2026 output per developer, with a 1.46x preferred estimate after calendar controls. It is observational, covers one setting, and some alternative estimators shrink the effect. It still records a measured productivity gain. It says nothing about net ROI.

METR's 2025 randomised trial found developers were slower with AI. The observations come from before the target period, and the page itself marks them out of date. It shows that benefits vary by setting.

reviews.rationale: The claim flatly denies any measurable productivity benefit. A dated study of April 2026 measured higher developer output linked to AI adoption, which contradicts that flat denial. The study has real limits: it is observational, covers one favourable deployment, and some estimators are not significant. Financial ROI is not established, and the promises clause is not assessed.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The condition 'once OpenAI dies' comes correctly from the sentence before. The proposition drops 'profitability', a minor omission.

contract.note: Reading 'impossible-to-answer' as a serious obstacle to financing is fair. The contract correctly requires a verified OpenAI collapse before the claim can be scored.

evidence.note: OpenAI's 28 Oct 2026 release notes show it still operating. This bears on the condition, not on the predicted financing outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast that depends on OpenAI dying. That had not happened by the evaluation date, so the forecast cannot be scored. With no deadline, it stays open.
